title: Control-plane rolling upgrade triggered token burst and circuit-breaker oscillation — postmortem & action tracker
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a scheduled control-plane rolling upgrade in primary region (us-west-2), a transient configuration skew caused a sudden increase in token accounting for routed requests. The secondary region (eu-west-1), which became the active failover target for a subset of traffic, experienced a burst of token consumption that triggered heterogeneous circuit breaker oscillation and aggressive load-shedding. Result: a sustained 12-minute SLO miss for 95th/99th latency on text-generation and a degraded throughput window for several customers. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied in the incident, and tracked follow-up actions.
impact_summary: 12-minute SLO miss for gen endpoints; ~320k extra tokens billed and ~3% request drop rate for affected customers between 2026-03-10T03:42 and 2026-03-10T03:54 UTC. Several enterprise Dedicated clusters saw elevated tail latency; onboarding customers observed API 429 bursts.
timeline: 2026-03-10T03:30 UTC — Control-plane rolling upgrade begins in us-west-2 (scheduled maintenance).
2026-03-10T03:38 UTC — One control-plane instance applied new feature flag that temporarily changed token accounting multiplier for routed proxies.

2026-03-10T03:41 UTC — Traffic routing shifted 18% of active queues to eu-west-1 due to planned shard migration. Observability alert: token-rate spike in eu-west-1 (teams relied on control-plane metric stream).
2026-03-10T03:42 UTC — eu-west-1 circuit breakers for high-priority queues began tripping and recovering repeatedly (oscillation), triggering load-shedding policies.
2026-03-10T03:45 UTC — On-call team opened incident, rolled back the control-plane flag in us-west-2. Immediate token-rate delta reduced but CB oscillation persisted due to stale KV cache warmups.
2026-03-10T03:54 UTC — Circuit breaker hysteresis adjusted manually and KV prefixes warmed; SLOs recovered and load normalised. Post-incident monitoring continued for 6 hours.
2026-03-10T10:00 UTC — Initial postmortem draft created and assigned to engineering resilience squad.
root_cause: A control-plane feature flag in the rolling upgrade temporarily altered token accounting multiplier used by the routing proxy. The multiplier increase, combined with a synchronized shard migration, produced a concentrated token burst to secondary region. The secondary region's circuit-breaker hysteresis parameters were tuned for steady-state traffic and lacked damping for a rapid multi-queue token spike, causing CB oscillation. KV cache cold state in the secondary region amplified latency, prolonging the recovery window.
contributing_factors: Rolling upgrade applied new accounting flag without gradual ramp or canary that exercised cross-region routing scenarios.
Shard migration schedule aligned with maintenance window; lack of decoupling produced combined load peak.
Circuit-breaker hysteresis and recovery backoff parameters tuned for throughput, not for rapid transient multipliers.
KV cache warmup on failover paths was cold and relied on reactive warmup rather than proactive prefix seeding.
Runbooks did not include a quick rollback knob for the specific control-plane flag; on-call needed to coordinate with release owner.
what_we_did_during_incident: Rolled back control-plane flag in us-west-2 (03:45 UTC).
Adjusted circuit-breaker hysteresis (increased recovery backoff + added minimum cooldown window) to stop oscillation (03:50 UTC).
Manually pre-warmed critical KV prefixes for top 10 tenants in eu-west-1.
Opened emergency routing guard to throttle new shard migrations until stability confirmed.
Launched post-incident monitoring dashboard to track token-rate deltas and CB state across regions.
short_term_mitigations: Add a temporary safety gate that prevents applying token-accounting-affecting flags while large shard migrations are in flight.
Implement automatic damping in CB controller to detect high-frequency trip/recover cycles and apply exponential backoff for recovery attempts.
Proactive KV prefix seeding for failover targets before maintenance windows (scripted task).
long_term_remediations: Introduce canary policy that simulates cross-region routing for every control-plane flag that touches accounting/routing logic; require green canary before full rollout.
Revise circuit-breaker controller to incorporate token-rate derivatives (delta and acceleration) into trip/backoff decisions, not just absolute token rate.
Create scheduling constraints for shard migrations to avoid overlap with control-plane upgrades for the same region pair by default.
Enhance runbooks with a documented rollback command for accounting flags and an on-call escalation path to release owner + product manager.
action_items: ENG-866001: Implement canary gating for token-accounting flags (owner: Priya Ramachandran, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-866002: Add CB oscillation detector + exponential recovery backoff in CB controller (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2026-04-07)
ENG-866003: Proactive KV prefix seeding job and maintenance pre-warm playbook (owner: Wei Zhang, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-866004: Migration-or-upgrade scheduler constraints proposal and rollout (owner: Sasha Ivanov, due: 2026-04-14)
ENG-866005: Runbook update — rollback commands + communication recipe (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-866006: Billing reconciliation and customer outreach for token overcharge (owner: Customer Success: Lina Gomez, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-866007: Post-change automated QA test that simulates coin-flip cross-region routing under control-plane flags (owner: Resilience QA: Devon Park, due: 2026-04-01)
postmortem_notes_and_decisions: Decision: No immediate change to circuit-breaker defaults in runtime-1.28; we'll ship detector + backoff in runtime-1.29 after validation.
Decision: All future control-plane releases that touch accounting will require a cross-region canary for at least 30 minutes under low-traffic hours.
We accepted short-term temporary guard to prevent migrations during control-plane rollouts as an operational policy (until scheduler constraints are implemented).
Customer outreach: CS to refund or credit customers affected by token overcharge; communications will be templated to include incident timeline and mitigation steps.
